headings.title: Creation of department and program transfers
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Department of Health and Senior Services, directs supervision of public health functions, abolishes the division of health, and transfers listed agencies and programs (source footnotes note name change to Children's Special Health Care Needs Service and repeals of 191.500-191.550 and 199.070).

headings.title: Administration of Older Americans Act duties
headings.reviewNote: Transfers Older Americans Act responsibilities to the department by type I transfer and designates the department as the sole agency to develop and coordinate the state plan.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Department of Health and Senior Services, transfers public health functions and programs, and transfers Older Americans Act responsibilities.

headings.title: Appointment and tenure of department director
headings.reviewNote: Provides for gubernatorial appointment of the director with senate consent, specifies tenure at the governor's pleasure, and caps salary at appropriations.

headings.title: Qualifications and experience of department director
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes character, educational accreditation, administrative experience, and public health management requirements for the department director.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs the appointment, tenure, compensation limit, and professional qualifications of the director of health and senior services.

headings.title: Environmental health monitoring and recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to monitor environmental health effects, prepare population risk assessments, and make recommendations to natural resources.

headings.title: Comprehensive disease prevention plan development
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to develop a disease prevention plan expanding programs and consulting with health insurers regarding medical care cost effectiveness.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs environmental health hazard monitoring and population risk assessments, and requires development of a disease prevention plan.

headings.title: Establishment of putative father registry
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to establish a putative father registry recording adjudicated fathers and persons filing notices of intent to claim paternity.

headings.title: Filing of acknowledgment affidavit form
headings.reviewNote: Requires persons filing a notice of intent or acknowledgment of paternity to use the state registrar's affidavit form meeting federal minimum standards.

headings.title: Notice of change of address
headings.reviewNote: Requires any person filing a notice of intent to claim paternity to notify the registry of address changes.

headings.title: Revocation of paternity claim notice
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes revocation of a filed notice of intent at any time and renders the revoked notice a nullity nunc pro tunc upon receipt.

headings.title: Admissibility of unrevoked paternity notice
headings.reviewNote: Allows an unrevoked notice of intent to claim paternity to be introduced into evidence by any other party in relevant proceedings.

headings.title: Lack of knowledge of pregnancy
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that lack of knowledge of pregnancy does not excuse failure to timely file under adoption consent provisions.

headings.title: Waiver of adoption consent and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that failure to timely file waives adoption consent rights unless mother's fraud or misrepresentation occurred and filing follows within fifteen days.

headings.title: Confidentiality and disclosure of registry records
headings.reviewNote: Requires release of registry information within two business days to courts or authorized adoption entities and restricts other disclosures without court order.

headings.title: Forms and public education materials
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to prepare registration forms, publish explanatory pamphlets, and distribute public service announcements regarding the registry.

headings.title: Mandatory statement in informational publications
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department's prepared informational statement to be included in any pamphlet or publication informing the public about the registry.

headings.title: Establishment of Putative Father Registry Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the dedicated Putative Father Registry Fund in the state treasury, directs deposit of fees, and prohibits fund balance reversion.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes and regulates the putative father registry, notice of paternity claims, evidentiary rules, adoption consent waivers, and registry funding.

headings.title: Disease prevention authority and regulatory orders
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to safeguard public health, study causes and prevention of diseases, designate dangerous communicable diseases, and issue preventive orders.

headings.title: Mandatory communicable disease reporting list
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to include MRSA, specified CRE, VRE, and alpha-gal syndrome in its list of reportable communicable or infectious diseases.

headings.title: Alpha-gal syndrome reporting and confidentiality
headings.reviewNote: Requires laboratory reporting of alpha-gal test results within seven days, authorizes sample follow-ups and federal reports, and restricts disclosure of identifiable records.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes department duties regarding communicable disease prevention, mandatory reporting lists, and alpha-gal syndrome laboratory reporting.

headings.title: Title of Lyme disease eradication act
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory citation as the Missouri Lyme Disease Eradication Act for sections 103.190 and 192.026 to 192.029.

headings.title: Definitions for Lyme disease eradication
headings.reviewNote: Defines department, Lyme disease, medically necessary, and posttreatment Lyme disease syndrome for eradication act sections.

headings.title: Lyme disease case reporting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Mandates provider and laboratory reporting of Lyme disease within three days and provides patient opt-in for sharing identifiable information.

headings.title: Annual report on Lyme disease incidence
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to compile and submit an annual report on Lyme disease incidence, demographics, and barriers to the CDC, legislature, and public website.

headings.title: Academic collaboration for surveillance integration
headings.reviewNote: Directs department collaboration with public four-year higher education institutions to integrate Lyme disease surveillance into monitoring programs.

headings.title: Privacy protection for reported data
headings.reviewNote: Requires all data collected or reported under Lyme disease provisions to protect identifiable information consistent with privacy laws.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department rulemaking to implement Lyme disease eradication provisions subject to chapter 536 nonseverability requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Missouri Lyme Disease Eradication Act, defining terms, mandating case reporting, requiring surveillance reports, and granting rulemaking authority.

headings.title: Establishment of Lyme Research and Eradication Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the dedicated Lyme Research and Eradication Fund in the state treasury, specifies authorized uses, and directs investment earnings to the fund without biennial reversion under section 33.080.

headings.title: Distribution of research and eradication grants
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to distribute fund moneys for research grants to higher education, research institutions, and nonprofits for diagnostic, therapy, and eradication projects.

headings.title: Minimum fund allocation for rural counties
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that at least twenty percent of research fund moneys be utilized to support Lyme disease eradication efforts in rural counties.

headings.title: Annual legislative report on fund expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to submit an annual report to the general assembly by March first detailing expenditures, research outcomes, and eradication progress.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Lyme Research and Eradication Fund, allocates research and eradication grants, mandates minimum rural county funding, and requires an annual legislative report.

headings.title: Establishment and composition of task force
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Lyme Disease Task Force within the department and specifies membership including the director, physicians, nurses, local health administrator, veterinarian, and diagnosed residents.

headings.title: Member terms and meeting schedule
headings.reviewNote: Sets three-year member terms, provides for vacancy appointments, requires at least semiannual meetings, and authorizes expense reimbursement without compensation.

headings.title: Duties and responsibilities of task force
headings.reviewNote: Assigns task force duties to monitor eradication act implementation, review diagnostic literature, recommend professional education, and assist in information sharing policies.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates the Lyme Disease Task Force, specifying member composition, terms, meetings, expense reimbursement, and advisory duties.

headings.title: Hepatitis C protocols and screening guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to use National Institutes of Health hepatitis C protocols for provider education and permits guidelines including acute/chronic tracking, a line-item prison screening plan, and a one-year report.

headings.title: Appropriation contingency for hepatitis C duties
headings.reviewNote: Conditions performance of hepatitis C education and screening duties upon specific appropriations by the general assembly.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires adoption of national guidelines for hepatitis C education and screening protocols, subject to appropriations.

headings.title: Department access to patient medical records
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to receive patient medical record information for epidemiological studies and applies access to infection and maternal mortality data.

headings.title: Confidentiality and restricted release of records
headings.reviewNote: Requires strict confidentiality of abstracted medical records and restricts release to statistical aggregate forms or authorized public health coinvestigators.

headings.title: Immunity for disclosing confidential information
headings.reviewNote: Protects individuals and organizations providing medical record information from civil or criminal liability absent bad faith or malicious purpose.

headings.title: Reimbursement for data abstracting costs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department reimbursement to medical care facilities for costs of abstracting data for special studies within appropriations.

headings.title: Criminal penalty for unauthorized release
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowing release of confidential medical record information by employees, authorities, or coinvestigators as a class A misdemeanor.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes receipt of patient medical records for epidemiological studies and infection data, establishes confidentiality protections, and provides civil immunity.

headings.title: Managed care data submission requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires entities subject to sections 354.400 to 354.636 to submit quality of care, access, satisfaction, and health status data, subject to section 354.444 penalties and potential exclusion from state health programs.

headings.title: Data standards and collection rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to specify reporting data by rule, permitting reliance on national accreditation standards, HEDIS sets, and agency consultations.

headings.title: Confidentiality of submitted data and reports
headings.reviewNote: Classifies submitted raw data as nonpublic, authorizes public aggregate comparative reports identifying entities, and protects patient identity from release.

headings.title: Publication of consumer guide and fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires publication of an annual consumer guide after entity review and allows reasonable fees for specialized reports credited to the public health services fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates health maintenance organization quality and access reporting to the department, data standards, confidentiality, and consumer guide publication.

headings.title: Development of childhood immunization materials
headings.reviewNote: Directs the bureau of immunization to develop educational materials recommending childhood vaccines including Hib, hepatitis B, and tuberculin tests.

headings.title: Distribution of educational materials and risk disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Requires distribution of vaccine materials through hospitals, health units, and parent education programs, incorporating federal risk disclosures and consent rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs the bureau of immunization to develop and distribute educational materials on recommended childhood vaccines and risk disclosures.

headings.title: Definitions for food donation protections
headings.reviewNote: Defines canned food, donor, food, hermetically sealed container, perishable food, and prepared food for statutory donation provisions.

headings.title: Authorization to donate surplus food
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes commercial food facilities and retailers to make excess canned and perishable food available to bona fide charitable entities to feed individuals in need.

headings.title: Donor immunity from civil and criminal liability
headings.reviewNote: Shields good faith food donors from criminal penalties and civil damages regarding food condition absent gross negligence, recklessness, or intentional misconduct.

headings.title: Charitable distributor immunity from liability
headings.reviewNote: Protects bona fide charitable organizations and volunteer distributors from civil and criminal liability when handling and distributing donated food in good faith.

headings.title: Annual department information on food-recovery programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to make available and annually update information on the need and benefits of food-recovery programs, how organizations may participate, and existing food-recovery entities or food banks.

entries.reviewSummary: Defines food donation terms, authorizes surplus food donations, provides good-faith civil and criminal liability protections for donors and charitable distributors, and requires annual food-recovery information.

headings.title: Patient inquiries on bone marrow registry
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes primary care and urgent care physicians to inquire about bone marrow registry status for adult patients under forty-five and provide educational materials.

headings.title: Department development of educational materials
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to develop informational materials explaining the need for bone marrow donation, patient populations, registry enrollment, and swab kits.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants the department rulemaking authority to implement registry education provisions subject to chapter 536 nonseverability requirements.

headings.title: Cost-effective dissemination of registry materials
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes oral, print, or electronic dissemination of bone marrow materials provided the department determines the method is cost effective for providers.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes primary care and urgent care provider inquiries on bone marrow registry status, requires educational materials, and establishes rulemaking authority.

headings.title: Definitions for infection reporting
headings.reviewNote: Defines antibiogram, antimicrobial, and department for healthcare-associated infection reporting provisions.

headings.title: Laboratory reporting of culture and sensitivity data
headings.reviewNote: Requires Missouri laboratories performing culture and sensitivity testing to submit healthcare-associated infection data including antibiograms and MRSA or VRE isolates.

headings.title: Confidentiality and licensure authority disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Protects reported infection information under confidentiality laws while making provider-specific records available to appropriate facility licensing authorities.

headings.title: Infection tracking and surveillance system
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to establish a surveillance system tracking preventable infections and monitoring antibiotic resistance trends in pathogens.

headings.title: Compliance with federal reporting guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to conform infection reporting implementation to guidelines and standards adopted by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes laboratory reporting of healthcare-associated infection data, confidentiality standards, and a surveillance system for antibiotic-resistant microbes.

headings.title: Transfer of Division of Aging and duties
headings.reviewNote: Transfers the Division of Aging to the department by type I transfer to assist elderly and disabled adults and regulate long-term care facilities.

headings.title: Department duties for elderly and long-term care programs
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates nineteen department duties including Older Americans Act administration, information and referral, area agency allocations, Title XVIII/XIX facility surveys and certification, dementia clearinghouse, social services contracts, and Patient Self-Determination Act monitoring.

headings.title: Withdrawal of area agency on aging designation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes withdrawal of an area agency on aging designation for noncompliance, misuse of funds, or inadequate services after consultation, provides appeals to the director and governor, and requires interim department administration.

headings.title: Orientation and continuing education for facility inspectors
headings.reviewNote: Requires chapter 198 inspection personnel hired after August 13, 1988 to complete at least one hundred hours of basic orientation in their first six months and twenty hours of annual continuing education.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department rulemaking for specified aging and adult-protection sections subject to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with nonseverability for rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2001.

headings.title: Home and community based services program description
headings.reviewNote: Describes the department-operated home and community based services program that informs individuals of available long-term care options.

headings.title: Minimum dementia-specific training for care employees
headings.reviewNote: Requires minimum dementia-specific orientation and in-service training for direct-care and daily-contact employees and independent contractors of long-term care, in-home, adult day care, home health, and hospice providers (source footnote notes residential care facilities may include assisted living facilities).

entries.reviewSummary: Transfers the Division of Aging to the department, enumerates elderly and long-term care duties, regulates area agency withdrawal, inspector training, rulemaking, home and community based services, and dementia-specific training.

headings.title: Establishment of shared care program
headings.reviewNote: Creates the shared care program within the department to support family caregivers caring for elderly persons at home to prevent institutionalization.

headings.title: Department duties in administering shared care
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to register caregivers, develop physician and staff certification forms, provide resource coordination, and explain tax credit guidelines.

headings.title: Administration of shared care program funds
headings.reviewNote: Directs that funds appropriated for the shared care program be appropriated to and administered by the department.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the shared care program to support family caregiving for elderly persons and specifies department administrative duties and funding.

headings.title: Caregiver eligibility for shared care tax credit
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes an individual tax credit up to five hundred dollars for uncompensated registered caregivers residing with dependent elderly individuals needing facility-level care.

headings.title: Tax year applicability for shared care credit
headings.reviewNote: Applies the shared care tax credit to tax years beginning after December 31, 1999.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to implement shared care tax credit provisions subject to chapter 536 nonseverability requirements.

headings.title: Penalties for falsifying tax credit documents
headings.reviewNote: Subjects persons who knowingly falsify documents required for the shared care tax credit to the same penalties as falsifying other tax documents under chapter 143.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes caregiver eligibility requirements for the shared care tax credit, tax year applicability, rulemaking authority, and fraud penalties.

headings.title: Area agency governance and annual performance reports
headings.reviewNote: Establishes area agency on aging governance over Title III funds, requires director appointments, and mandates detailed annual performance and financial reporting.

headings.title: Duties of area agency advisory council
headings.reviewNote: Specifies advisory council responsibilities regarding policy guidelines, area plan and budget review, effectiveness evaluations, and open quarterly meetings.

headings.title: Powers and duties of area agency boards
headings.reviewNote: Delineates area agency board duties including planning, assessing elderly needs, contracting for services, monitoring providers, and reporting fiscal data.

headings.title: Biennial audit requirement for area agencies
headings.reviewNote: Mandates biennial audits of each area agency on aging and provides that federal Older Americans Act audits satisfy this requirement.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs area agency on aging operations, annual performance reporting, advisory council responsibilities, board duties, and biennial audit requirements.

headings.title: Budget allotment schedule and area plan hearings
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual department budget allotments by January, area plan submissions by March, local public hearings in April, and findings reported within thirty days.

headings.title: Annual performance measures and outcome targets
headings.reviewNote: Requires area agencies to include performance measures and annual outcome targets in area plans presented at public hearings.

headings.title: Annual on-site monitoring and report distribution
headings.reviewNote: Mandates annual on-site department monitoring of each area agency and transmission of reports to advisory councils and governing boards.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes budget allotment schedules, area plan submissions, public hearings, annual outcome measures, and annual on-site monitoring of area agencies.

headings.title: Alzheimer's disease pilot project grant authorization
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes grants to public and private entities for pilot projects to delay institutionalization and provide respite for Alzheimer's patients and families.

headings.title: Rulemaking for Alzheimer's grant procedures
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director to promulgate administrative rules establishing application, review, selection, monitoring, and auditing procedures for Alzheimer's pilot grants.

headings.title: Duration and renewal of pilot grants
headings.reviewNote: Limits pilot project grants to a duration of one year and permits renewal for one additional year subject to appropriations and director discretion.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes pilot project grants for Alzheimer's disease services, directs rulemaking for grant administration, and limits grant duration.

headings.title: Establishment of dementia services coordinator position
headings.reviewNote: Creates a full-time dementia services coordinator position within the division of senior and disability services.

headings.title: Duties and responsibilities of dementia coordinator
headings.reviewNote: Delineates coordinator duties including evaluating services, coordinating resources, streamlining state programs, supporting training, and monitoring impact data.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates the position of dementia services coordinator within the division of senior and disability services and defines the coordinator's duties.

headings.title: License requirement for adult day care
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits establishing, operating, or advertising an adult day care program without obtaining the proper state license.

headings.title: Application procedures and fee schedule
headings.reviewNote: Requires adult day care license applications on department forms including the prescribed fee schedule.

headings.title: Attestation and document submission requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to submit all mandatory documentation and attest by signature that statements are true and correct.

headings.title: Filing of replacement and amendatory documents
headings.reviewNote: Requires program operators to file copies of replacement or amended documents within ten working days of their effective date.

headings.title: Concealment and failure to file documents
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes license revocation or application disapproval when failure to file documents is part of a pattern of concealment.

headings.title: Application review and license issuance criteria
headings.reviewNote: Directs department review and inspections, and mandates license issuance upon substantial compliance, background clearance, and fee payment.

headings.title: Validity period of adult day care license
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an adult day care license shall be valid for a designated period not exceeding two years from issuance.

headings.title: Written notice of license denial grounds
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to notify an applicant in writing of license denial stating specific reasons and statutory grounds.

headings.title: Contents and specifications of program license
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that issued licenses must state the operator, program name, facility location, operating hours, capacity, and validity period.

headings.title: Issuance of temporary operating permits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes temporary operating permits for license renewal when state review is delayed through no fault of the applicant.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes licensing requirements, application procedures, qualification standards, license contents, and temporary operating permits for adult day care programs.

headings.title: Exit interviews and deficiency reporting procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires exit interviews, immediate written notices of class I violations, written deficiency reports, and formal correction orders within ten working days.

headings.title: Submission and review of correction plans
headings.reviewNote: Establishes timelines for operators to submit correction plans and for the department to approve or reject plans.

headings.title: Unannounced reinspections for cited deficiencies
headings.reviewNote: Mandates unannounced reinspections within specified statutory timeframes based on the classification severity of cited violations.

headings.title: Classification of adult day care standards
headings.reviewNote: Categorizes regulatory standards into class I imminent danger, class II direct health impact, and class III indirect impact.

headings.title: Public availability and redaction of reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires programs to make the most recent inspection report available to the public and authorizes redaction of identifiable health data.

headings.title: Documentation in lieu of on-site reinspection
headings.reviewNote: Permits waiving an on-site revisit when an adult day care program submits satisfactory documentation establishing correction of a cited deficiency (source footnote notes nonexistent section '600.404' appears in original rolls).

headings.title: Issuance of notice of noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuance and certified delivery of a formal notice of noncompliance when deficiencies remain uncorrected after reinspection.

headings.title: Contents of notice of noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that notices of noncompliance must inform the operator that the department may seek any authorized legal action.

headings.title: Probationary license consent agreements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes consent agreements granting probationary licenses with compliance milestones and voluntary license surrender conditions.

headings.title: Posting and agency distribution of notices
headings.reviewNote: Requires posting of noncompliance notices and inspection reports on site and distribution to relevant federal, state, and local agencies.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates adult day care inspections, deficiency reporting, classification of safety standards, reinspection timelines, noncompliance notices, and consent agreements.

headings.title: Statutory grounds for license revocation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes license revocation for noncompliance with class I, class II, or imminent-danger aggregate class III standards, refusal of inspection or access, financial incapacity, facility-related felony convictions or pleas, or employee disqualification listing.

headings.title: Written notice requirements for revocation
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice of revocation specifying grounds and delivery by certified mail or personal service at least ten calendar days prior to effective date.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes statutory grounds and written notice requirements for the revocation of an adult day care program license.

headings.title: Programs exempt from adult day care licensing
headings.reviewNote: Exempts programs operating two hours or less, federal facilities, relative care, programs with four or fewer clients, mental health facilities, and religious programs.

headings.title: Voluntary application for exempt programs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes exempt programs to voluntarily apply for and receive an adult day care license upon complying with statutory standards.

entries.reviewSummary: Exempts specified adult care programs from licensing requirements while preserving voluntary licensure eligibility.

headings.title: Right of entry and annual unannounced inspections
headings.reviewNote: Grants the department entry during operating hours for compliance and complaint investigations, mandating at least one unannounced inspection annually.

headings.title: Operator cooperation during inspections and investigations
headings.reviewNote: Requires license applicants and holders to cooperate with inspections by providing full access to premises, records, and personnel.

headings.title: Sanctions for failure to cooperate with inspections
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that failure to comply with lawful department requests during investigations constitutes grounds to refuse or revoke a license.

headings.title: Delegation of inspection authority to local entities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to designate competent political subdivision instrumentalities to investigate and inspect program facilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes department inspection and entry rights for adult day care programs, mandates cooperation, and permits local agency delegation.

headings.title: Investigation of unlicensed programs and warrants
headings.reviewNote: Directs department investigation of suspected unlicensed or noncompliant adult day care programs and authorizes circuit court orders for entry upon reasonable grounds if access is denied.

headings.title: Injunctive relief against unlawful program operations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to seek injunctive relief against adult day care programs operating in violation of statutory provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes investigations of unlicensed adult day care programs, court warrants for entry, and injunctive relief against violations.

headings.title: Administrative appeal of license refusal or revocation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes aggrieved persons to appeal license denial or revocation to the administrative hearing commission within thirty calendar days of notice.

headings.title: Administrative stay standards and safety exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes conditional stays of license revocation while prohibiting stays if imminent danger exists or where a license application was refused.

headings.title: Final administrative decisions and judicial review
headings.reviewNote: Vests final administrative decision authority with the commission and provides for judicial review in the court of appeals.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs administrative appeals of adult day care license refusals or revocations, stay standards, and judicial review procedures.

headings.title: Criminal penalties for adult day care violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violations and false statements as class A misdemeanors and elevates offenses involving abuse or neglect of participants to class E felonies.

headings.title: Mandatory license revocation and operating ban
headings.reviewNote: Mandates license revocation upon conviction and prohibits operating or holding a license for any adult day care program for three years.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes criminal penalties, felony upgrades for abuse or neglect, and mandatory three-year license disqualifications for violations.

headings.title: Website publication of adult day care inspections
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes website posting of adult day care inspection deficiencies and correction plans after dispute resolution.

headings.title: Federal health information privacy compliance
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that website disclosures shall not include information prohibited from disclosure under federal privacy laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes website publication of adult day care inspections and plans of correction while protecting confidential health data.

headings.title: Definitions for informal dispute resolution
headings.reviewNote: Defines deficiency, IDR, independent third party, and plan of correction for adult day care dispute resolution.

headings.title: Independent third party dispute resolution contracts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes contracts with Medicare quality organizations to conduct informal dispute resolution without formal evidentiary hearings or waiver of legal rights.

headings.title: Informal dispute resolution process and conferences
headings.reviewNote: Establishes timelines for deficiency statements, correction plans, and desk reviews, telephonic conferences, or face-to-face dispute conferences.

headings.title: Department written determination after IDR conference
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department, within ten calendar days of the IDR conference, to make a determination based on the facts and findings and transmit the decision and rationale in writing to the program.

headings.title: Transmission of revised statement of deficiencies
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to transmit a revised statement of deficiencies with the determination notice within ten calendar days of deciding to change the original statement.

headings.title: Submission of plan of correction after revision
headings.reviewNote: Requires the adult day care program to submit a plan of correction to the department within ten working days of receiving the determination and revised statement of deficiencies.

headings.title: Delay of website posting during pending dispute
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the department from posting disputed deficiency information on its website until the dispute determination is made and the program responds with a revised plan of correction, if needed.

headings.title: Administrative rulemaking compliance and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules created under this section to chapter 536 and section 536.028 and makes rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2014 nonseverable from legislative review powers.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes informal dispute resolution procedures for adult day care programs, third-party contracts, determination and revision timelines, website posting delays, and chapter 536 nonseverability.

headings.title: Establishment of Office of State Ombudsman
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Office of State Ombudsman for Long-Term Care Facility Residents to ensure care adequacy and quality of life.

headings.title: Administration by full-time state ombudsman
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the office shall be administered by a state ombudsman devoting entire time to statutory duties.

headings.title: Procedures for receiving and resolving complaints
headings.reviewNote: Directs establishment of procedures to receive, process, and resolve complaints affecting health, safety, and rights in long-term care facilities.

headings.title: Facility entry and resident record access
headings.reviewNote: Directs complaint resolution procedures and authorizes ombudsman entry into long-term care facilities and Missouri veterans' homes, resident access, record review with permission, and verification inquiries (source footnote notes 'homes' in original rolls).

headings.title: Complaint reporting and public outreach duties
headings.reviewNote: Requires the office to acknowledge complaints, report findings, make recommendations, disseminate materials, and publicize services.

headings.title: Legislative and regulatory policy recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes recommendations regarding agency rules and analysis of federal, state, and local laws affecting long-term care facilities.

headings.title: Promotion of community involvement and volunteers
headings.reviewNote: Directs the office to promote community involvement with facility residents through regional volunteer programs.

headings.title: Statewide policies and volunteer training standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires statewide regulations governing ombudsman activities and qualifications for regional coordinators and volunteers.

headings.title: Volunteer recruitment and training programs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes recruitment programs, training seminars, written materials, and publicity for ombudsman volunteers.

headings.title: Ombudsman authority to report abuse and neglect
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes regional coordinators and volunteers to report suspected abuse and neglect to the department ombudsman hotline.

headings.title: Administrator noncooperation reporting procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires notification of the state ombudsman when a nursing home administrator refuses to cooperate in resolving complaints.

headings.title: Preparation of informational ombudsman notices
headings.reviewNote: Directs the office to prepare written informational notices detailing office contact details, functions, and complaint procedures.

headings.title: Administrator distribution of notices to residents
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility administrators to provide ombudsman notices to every resident or guardian upon admission and during residency.

headings.title: Education of residents and families on legal rights
headings.reviewNote: Requires the office to inform residents, guardians, or families of their rights and entitlements under state and federal laws and regulations through educational materials and group meetings.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Office of State Ombudsman for Long-Term Care Facility Residents, defining powers, volunteer programs, resident access, and notices.

headings.title: Discretionary disclosure of files and identity limits
headings.reviewNote: Leaves disclosure of ombudsman program files to the ombudsman's discretion while barring disclosure of a complainant's or resident's identity without written consent or court order.

headings.title: Penalty for unauthorized disclosure and final result notice
headings.reviewNote: Classifies knowing and willful unauthorized disclosure of witness names or examination information by an office representative as a class A misdemeanor, while requiring disclosure of the final result to the facility with resident consent.

headings.title: Absolute privilege and immunity for statements and reports
headings.reviewNote: Grants absolute privilege and immunity from suit for relevant office statements or communications and for complaints or information provided in good faith.

headings.title: Exemption of office from court testimony on confidential matters
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the office shall not be required to testify in court on confidential matters except as necessary to enforce sections 192.2300 to 192.2315 or by court order.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates confidentiality and disclosure of ombudsman program files, criminal penalties for unauthorized disclosure, absolute privilege for good-faith reports, and testimony exemptions.

headings.title: Immunity from civil liability for ombudsmen
headings.reviewNote: Shields the state ombudsman, staff, and authorized volunteers from civil liability for official acts performed in good faith.

headings.title: Ban on retaliation and quality committee immunity
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits reprisal or retaliation against facility residents or employees for communicating with the office (class A misdemeanor) and grants good-faith civil immunity to federal quality assessment and assurance committee members.

entries.reviewSummary: Grants civil immunity and state-employee status to ombudsman staff and volunteers, prohibits reprisals against residents or employees, and shields quality assessment committee members.

headings.title: Mandatory reporting of eligible adult abuse
headings.reviewNote: Requires specified healthcare practitioners, law enforcement, first responders, and social services employees to report suspected abuse or neglect of eligible adults.

headings.title: Permissive reporting of adult abuse or neglect
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any other person who becomes aware of circumstances indicating abuse or neglect of an eligible adult to report to the department.

headings.title: Penalties for failure to make mandatory report
headings.reviewNote: References statutory penalties under criminal law for individuals who knowingly fail to report suspected abuse or neglect as required.

headings.title: Definition of first responder for reporting
headings.reviewNote: Defines first responder as personnel authorized to render emergency medical treatment, including police, sheriffs, firefighters, and EMTs.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes mandatory and permissive reporting of suspected abuse or neglect of eligible adults, penalties for failure to report, and defines first responder.

headings.title: Required contents of adult abuse reports
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that oral or written reports shall include identifying adult details, caregiver names, adult condition, and relevant facts.

headings.title: Referral of non-eligible adult reports
headings.reviewNote: Directs referral of reports concerning individuals who are not eligible adults to appropriate state or local authorities.

headings.title: Maintenance of statewide toll-free abuse hotline
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to maintain a statewide toll-free telephone hotline for receiving reports of suspected adult abuse and neglect.

entries.reviewSummary: Specifies information required in adult abuse reports, referral of non-eligible adult reports, and maintenance of a statewide reporting hotline.

headings.title: Confidentiality of adult abuse records and reports
headings.reviewNote: Classifies reports and records of adult abuse as confidential nonpublic records exempt from open records requirements.

headings.title: Authorized inspection and copying of abuse reports
headings.reviewNote: Restricts examination and copying of reports to the department, attorney general, mental health and social services departments for referred persons, law enforcement, multidisciplinary adult protection team members, and the eligible adult or guardian.

headings.title: Nondisclosure and release of reporter identity
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits disclosure of reporter identity without authorization or necessity to prevent harm, with exception for mental health investigations.

headings.title: Information sharing by adult protection teams
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes multidisciplinary adult protection teams to exchange necessary case records confidentially to perform official team functions.

headings.title: Penalty for unauthorized disclosure of records
headings.reviewNote: Classifies unauthorized dissemination of confidential abuse reports or central registry information as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Central registry maintenance and call recording
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to maintain a central registry and electronically record and retain incoming hotline reports for one year.

headings.title: Reporter identification efforts for anonymous calls
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to attempt to obtain the name and address of persons submitting reports to the central registry.

entries.reviewSummary: Protects confidentiality of adult abuse reports, regulates authorized access, reporter disclosure, multidisciplinary teams, and central registry records.

headings.title: Petition for involuntary adult protective services
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director to initiate chapter 202 or chapter 475 proceedings when an eligible adult cannot consent to protective services and presents a likelihood of serious physical harm (source footnote notes chapter 202 does not exist).

headings.title: Legal counsel retention for adult guardianship
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to retain legal counsel on a case-by-case basis to expedite adult guardianship and conservatorship proceedings.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes court petitions for involuntary adult protective services, probate hearings, and appointment of legal counsel in guardianship proceedings.

headings.title: Emergency peace officer medical transportation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes peace officers with probable cause of imminent harm to transport nonconsenting eligible adults to medical facilities and notify kin.

headings.title: Search warrants for barred access to adults
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes peace officers to apply for court warrants to enter premises and remove eligible adults when access is barred and harm is likely.

headings.title: Petitions for emergency court-ordered treatment
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director or medical facility head to petition for court-ordered treatment when authorized consent is absent or refused and staff find treatment necessary, while permitting prior emergency treatment if delay would jeopardize life.

headings.title: Appointment of guardian ad litem for treatment
headings.reviewNote: Requires prompt probate hearings and appointment of a guardian ad litem to determine and supervise emergency medical treatment.

headings.title: Mental health facility commitment limitation
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits rendering emergency care under this section in mental health facilities without civil commitment proceedings under chapter 632.

headings.title: Spiritual means and religious belief exemption
headings.reviewNote: Exempts individuals relying on spiritual means or prayer from mandatory medical treatment and from designation as eligible adults.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs emergency peace officer removal of eligible adults, court warrants, petitions for medical treatment, guardian ad litem appointment, and religious exemptions.

headings.title: Mandatory reporting of in-home client abuse
headings.reviewNote: Requires designated healthcare, adult day care, law enforcement, and social services professionals to report suspected abuse or neglect of in-home clients.

headings.title: Penalty for failure to report abuse
headings.reviewNote: Classifies failure to report suspected abuse or neglect of an in-home services client within a reasonable time as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Required contents of in-home abuse reports
headings.reviewNote: Specifies report details including provider agency, employee, client, home health agency, nature of abuse, and complainant identity.

headings.title: Permissive reporting of in-home client abuse
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any other person having reasonable cause to believe an in-home client or home health patient has been abused or neglected to report.

headings.title: Investigation and temporary protective orders
headings.reviewNote: Directs department investigation and authorizes ex parte circuit court orders for temporary care and protection not exceeding thirty days.

headings.title: Confidentiality of in-home abuse reports
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that reports of in-home client abuse or neglect shall be confidential under statutory provisions.

headings.title: Immunity from liability for making reports
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil and criminal immunity for reporting or testifying, except for abusers, perjury, or persons acting negligently, recklessly, in bad faith, or with malicious purpose.

headings.title: Written notification to reporting party
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notification to the reporting person within five working days of receipt of a required report and of the initiation of the investigation.

headings.title: Prohibition on employer retaliation against reporters
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits persons with authority in an in-home services provider or home health agency from harassing, dismissing, or retaliating against clients, patients, or employees who report suspected violations.

headings.title: Criminal prosecution for client abuse or neglect
headings.reviewNote: Subjects any person who abuses or neglects an in-home client or home health patient to criminal prosecution under statutory provisions.

headings.title: Quality assurance and supervision procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to establish client quality assurance processes requiring in-home providers to maintain direct supervision plans.

headings.title: Maintenance of employee disqualification list
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to maintain the employee disqualification list and list individuals found to have abused or neglected clients.

headings.title: Safe at home evaluation and nurse-authorized care plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires a department safe at home evaluation developed by chapter 536 rule, a nurse-authorized care plan (with optional licensed provider nurse assessment), and permissive interagency input and mental health referrals.

headings.title: Bi-annual registered nurse assessment visits
headings.reviewNote: Requires authorized registered nurse visits at least twice annually to assess in-home clients, service plans, and personal care workers.

headings.title: Advisement of client rights and complaint process
headings.reviewNote: Requires advising in-home services clients of their rights at initial evaluation, including the right to call the department for dissatisfaction, and directs establishing a non-abuse complaint process separate from the abuse hotline.

headings.title: Reimbursement of authorized nurse visits
headings.reviewNote: Provides that authorized nurse visits shall be reimbursed to in-home provider agencies subject to legislative appropriations.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates reporting of in-home services client abuse or neglect, investigations, ex parte protection orders, employee disqualification listing, and client rights.

headings.title: Reporting misappropriation of client property or records
headings.reviewNote: Permits any person with reasonable cause to believe an in-home services client's property or funds were misappropriated or service delivery documents falsified to report to the department.

headings.title: Required identifying information in misappropriation reports
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to obtain identifying information of provider agencies, employees, clients, and complainants for misappropriation reports.

headings.title: Criminal penalties for misappropriation of property
headings.reviewNote: Classifies diversion of an in-home services client's personal property or funds or falsification of service delivery documents by a provider agency or employee as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Investigation and referral to law enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Directs immediate investigation of misappropriation reports and referral of findings to appropriate law enforcement authorities.

headings.title: Department director review of misappropriation findings
headings.reviewNote: Requires investigator referral of probable misappropriation findings to the department director for administrative determination and legal action.

headings.title: Confidentiality of misappropriation reports and records
headings.reviewNote: Classifies reports and records of property misappropriation as confidential nonpublic records pursuant to statute.

headings.title: Immunity from liability for reporting misappropriation
headings.reviewNote: Grants civil and criminal immunity for reporting or testifying, except for participants/beneficiaries of misappropriation, perjury, or negligent, reckless, bad-faith, or malicious conduct.

headings.title: Written notice to reporting person
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notification to the reporting person within five working days of receipt of a report and of the initiation of the investigation.

headings.title: Prohibition on retaliation by provider agencies
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits in-home provider agencies from harassing, dismissing, or retaliating against employees who report misappropriation or testify.

headings.title: Employee disqualification listing for property misappropriation
headings.reviewNote: Directs placement of persons on the employee disqualification list who have misappropriated client funds or falsified service records.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes reporting, criminal penalties, employer retaliation bans, and employee disqualification listing for misappropriation of in-home client funds.

headings.title: Administrative appeal of in-home contract sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes in-home provider contractors to appeal proposed contract denial, suspension, probation, or termination to the administrative hearing commission.

headings.title: Issuance of warning letters without hearing
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to issue letters of censure or warning to in-home providers without formal administrative notice or hearing.

headings.title: Stay of contract sanctions pending hearing
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the administrative hearing commission to stay contract suspension, probation, or termination pending final decision upon finding no client danger.

headings.title: Minimum operating conditions during administrative stay
headings.reviewNote: Requires as a minimum condition of any administrative hearing commission stay that the contractor operate under the same contractual requirements and regulations applicable to all other program contractors.

headings.title: Evidentiary standard and scope of review
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that the administrative hearing commission shall evaluate circumstances existing at the time of department action.

headings.title: Burden of proof on appealing contractor
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that the appealing in-home contractor or applicant bears the burden of proof in proceedings before the commission.

headings.title: Final decision and judicial review in court
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any aggrieved person, including the department, to seek judicial review of a final administrative hearing commission decision as provided in section 621.145.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs administrative appeals to the Administrative Hearing Commission for in-home services provider contract sanctions and judicial review.

headings.title: Notice of intent to list employee
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice mailed to the last known address of a person determined for employee disqualification listing, stating the allegation, listing consequences and duration, and challenge procedures.

headings.title: Inclusion on list upon failure to reply
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes inclusion on the employee disqualification list if no hearing request is received within thirty days of mailing notice.

headings.title: Application for administrative hearing
headings.reviewNote: Provides that an individual may challenge proposed listing by filing a written application for an administrative hearing within thirty days.

headings.title: Reopening listing for lack of notice
headings.reviewNote: Allows a person listed without required subsection 1 notice to request removal or a hearing, requiring the department within thirty days of receipt either to remove the name or grant a hearing.

headings.title: Conduct of administrative hearing in county
headings.reviewNote: Requires hearings to be conducted in the individual's county of residence by the department director or designated hearing officer.

headings.title: Administrative determination on hearing record
headings.reviewNote: Directs the director or designee to decide all questions presented based on the hearing record and issue written findings of fact.

headings.title: Notice of right to seek judicial review
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to notify aggrieved individuals of their right to seek judicial review under administrative procedure laws.

headings.title: Inadmissibility of director decision in civil suits
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that the director's administrative determination is inadmissible in civil actions brought against facilities or provider agencies.

headings.title: Duration of listing on disqualification list
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the director shall determine the duration of an individual's listing on the employee disqualification list.

headings.title: Record retention following removal from list
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes retention of historical records regarding substantiated acts even after an individual's name is removed from the active list.

headings.title: Provision of disqualification list to authorized entities
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to provide the disqualification list to other state agencies, health facilities, providers, and authorized employers upon request.

headings.title: Ban on employing listed persons and employer immunity
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits listed recipient entities from knowingly employing anyone on the employee disqualification list and grants immunity from suit for declining to employ or terminating a listed person.

headings.title: Immunity and unemployment charge exemption for required discharge
headings.reviewNote: Shields employers and vendors required by law to deny employment or discharge an employee based on background checks, disqualification registries, or waiver denial from discharge liability and section 288.100 unemployment charges.

headings.title: Petition for removal from disqualification list
headings.reviewNote: Permits listed individuals to submit a written removal request to the director at most once every twelve months, grantable upon a clear written showing with optional conditions and no right of appeal.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates employee disqualification list procedures, notices, administrative hearings, disclosure requirements, and removal petitions.

headings.title: Definition of provider for background checks
headings.reviewNote: Defines provider for background check requirements including health care facilities, home health agencies, hospice, and in-home providers.

headings.title: Definition of patient or resident
headings.reviewNote: Incorporates the definition of patient or resident from section 43.539 (source footnote notes revisor update from 43.540 in 2019).

headings.title: Pre-employment criminal and disqualification checks
headings.reviewNote: Requires providers or employment agencies, before allowing patient or resident contact, to request a section 43.540 highway patrol criminal check (plus nationwide fingerprint check if under five years in Missouri) and an employee disqualification list inquiry.

headings.title: Reimbursement of background check costs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes providers requesting criminal history record checks through the highway patrol to require applicants to reimburse actual check costs.

headings.title: Applicant consent forms and criminal disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants for patient contact positions to sign consent forms disclosing full criminal history and disqualifying backgrounds.

headings.title: Misdemeanors for nondisclosure and improper hiring
headings.reviewNote: Classifies an applicant's knowing failure to disclose criminal history and a provider's knowing hiring or retention of a person found guilty of specified class A or B felonies or abuse offenses as class A misdemeanors.

headings.title: Criminal penalty for provider employing disqualified persons
headings.reviewNote: Classifies an in-home or home health agency's knowing employment of a person refusing family care safety registry registration or having listed disqualifying convictions or registry findings as a class A misdemeanor (source footnote notes 'chapters' in original rolls).

headings.title: Examination of fingerprint background check protocols
headings.reviewNote: Directs the highway patrol to examine protocols enabling providers to request statewide fingerprint criminal background checks.

headings.title: Use of private investigatory background agencies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes providers to utilize qualified private investigatory agencies to conduct applicant criminal history checks in lieu of patrol checks.

headings.title: Hiring exemptions and good cause waivers
headings.reviewNote: Provides that general criminal hiring restrictions do not apply to applicants who have obtained departmental good cause waivers.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes criminal background checks, consent disclosures, disqualification screenings, and misdemeanor penalties for providers hiring direct care staff.

headings.title: Confidentiality of elder abuse and neglect reports
headings.reviewNote: Classifies abuse and neglect reports as confidential nonpublic records exempt from disclosure under public records laws.

headings.title: Disclosure of reports to employment security
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department, upon request, to provide the division of employment security copies of investigative reports that led to an employee's placement on the disqualification list.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes confidentiality protections and disclosure exceptions for elder abuse reports and requires providing disqualification investigative reports to the Division of Employment Security upon request.

headings.title: Mandatory animal abuse recognition training for workers
headings.reviewNote: Requires all personnel providing adult protective services to complete training on identifying and documenting animal abuse and neglect by December 2027.

headings.title: Interagency development of training curriculum
headings.reviewNote: Directs the departments of health and senior services and agriculture, by December 31, 2026 in consultation with the Missouri Animal Control Association or a successor entity, to develop or adapt available training materials.

headings.title: Training during working hours and continuing education
headings.reviewNote: Requires providing opportunities to complete required training during regular working hours and permits the training to qualify toward continuing education requirements.

headings.title: Definitions of animal and successor entity
headings.reviewNote: Defines animal as dogs, cats, rabbits, and domesticated birds, and defines successor entity for training program provisions.

headings.title: Statutory expiration of animal training requirements
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the animal abuse recognition training requirements shall expire on December 31, 2030.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates animal abuse and neglect recognition training for adult protective services workers, interagency curriculum development, and sunset date.

headings.title: Citation of Justice for Survivors Act
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory citation as the Justice for Survivors Act for section 192.2520 and section 197.135.

headings.title: Definitions for sexual assault examination network
headings.reviewNote: Defines appropriate medical provider, department, evidentiary collection kit, forensic examination, and telehealth for section 192.2520.

headings.title: Establishment of statewide forensic telehealth network
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a statewide telehealth network within the department to support forensic medical examinations for sexual assault victims.

headings.title: Mentoring and educational training services provided
headings.reviewNote: Requires the telehealth network to provide mentoring, trauma-informed training, and evidence collection guidance for medical providers.

headings.title: Online training and videoconferencing capabilities
headings.reviewNote: Directs that network training be made available online with videoconferencing connecting providers to interdisciplinary forensic experts.

headings.title: Continuous twenty-four-hour telehealth examination access
headings.reviewNote: Requires continuous twenty-four-hour telehealth consultation by sexual assault nurse examiners to guide treating medical providers during examinations.

headings.title: Interagency consultations and operational contracts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department consultations and contracts with government agencies, universities, hospitals, and clinics to operate the network.

headings.title: Mandatory annual hospital reporting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Requires licensed hospitals to report annually regarding sexual assault examination volume, provider staffing, and network utilization.

headings.title: Annual department public report on hospital data
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to publish an annual public report compiling hospital sexual assault examination data, staffing, and network usage.

headings.title: Appropriations, grants, and telehealth network fund
headings.reviewNote: Subjects network funding to appropriations, requires grant applications and allows gifts, and creates the dedicated Justice for Survivors Telehealth Network Fund in the state treasury.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority for forensic network operations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate rules establishing network standards, training protocols, and reporting requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Justice for Survivors Act, establishing a statewide telehealth network for sexual assault forensic examinations, hospital reporting, and rules.

headings.title: Licensing requirement for pediatric extended care
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits establishing, maintaining, or operating a prescribed pediatric extended care facility without obtaining a license from the department.

headings.title: Exemptions from pediatric extended care licensing
headings.reviewNote: Exempts child care facilities with at least a one-to-one licensed nurse ratio, hospitals or homes primarily providing medical, nursing, or convalescent care for children, and specified DMH-licensed programs.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits unlicensed operation of prescribed pediatric extended care facilities and specifies statutory exemptions.

headings.title: Department powers and pediatric facility standards
headings.reviewNote: Empowers the department to issue, inspect, suspend, or revoke licenses and promulgate standards for staffing, fire safety, sanitation, and records.

headings.title: Right of entry and inspection protocols
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes entry for announced compliance inspections on twenty-four hours' notice and unannounced inspections for child abuse investigations.

headings.title: Facility cooperation during inspections and investigations
headings.reviewNote: Requires license applicants and holders to cooperate with department investigations and inspections.

headings.title: Sanctions for failure to cooperate with inspections
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that failure to comply with lawful department requests during inspections constitutes grounds to refuse or revoke a license.

headings.title: Facility requests for regulatory variances
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes facilities to request written regulatory variances and prohibits department approval of any variance endangering child health or safety.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to implement pediatric extended care provisions subject to chapter 536 nonseverability requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Delineates department powers, inspections, facility standards, staff cooperation, variance requests, and rulemaking for pediatric extended care facilities.

headings.title: Child care licensing requirement for pediatric facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants and holders of pediatric extended care licenses to maintain an active child care facility license from elementary and secondary education.

headings.title: Child care staff compliance for pediatric employees
headings.reviewNote: Classifies all employees, contractors, and volunteers of pediatric extended care facilities as child care staff members subject to background screening laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Requires child care licensure and employee background compliance under education department standards for pediatric extended care facilities.

headings.title: Notice of proposed discipline and hearing rights
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice of proposed license denial, probation, or revocation, granting applicants thirty days to request an administrative hearing.

headings.title: Immediate suspension upon child care license suspension
headings.reviewNote: Mandates immediate suspension and proposed revocation of pediatric license if the licensee's child care license is immediately suspended.

headings.title: Immediate suspension upon child care license revocation
headings.reviewNote: Mandates immediate suspension and proposed revocation of pediatric license if the licensee's child care license is revoked by education authorities.

headings.title: Immediate suspension for imminent bodily harm
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes immediate license suspension simultaneously with disciplinary notice if the department finds a threat of imminent bodily harm to children.

headings.title: Notice of immediate suspension and appeal rights
headings.reviewNote: Requires notices of immediate suspension to specify factual grounds and inform licensees of appeal rights to the department within ten days.

headings.title: Judicial review of final department decisions
headings.reviewNote: Entitles any person aggrieved by a final department decision under sections 192.2550 to 192.2560 to judicial review as provided in chapter 536.

headings.title: Circuit court injunctive relief for imminent bodily harm
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department or attorney general to seek circuit court injunctive relief—including removing children, overseeing operation, or closing licensed or unlicensed non-exempt facilities—for imminent bodily harm, without civil liability for not filing suit.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs disciplinary notices, immediate license suspensions, department appeals, chapter 536 judicial review, and circuit court injunctive relief for prescribed pediatric extended care facilities.

headings.title: Confidentiality and restricted access to child records
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits public disclosure of confidential child records from pediatric extended care facilities, limiting access to specified agencies and guardians.

headings.title: Public availability of inspection and complaint reports
headings.reviewNote: Makes inspection reports and complaint investigation records accessible to the public provided complainant and child identities are protected.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes confidentiality protections for pediatric extended care child records and regulates public access to inspection reports.

headings.title: County health orders and agricultural standard restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes county commissions and health boards to issue public health orders, prohibiting conflicts with state rules or stricter agricultural standards.

headings.title: Establishment of county public health fees
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes reasonable county fees to support public health activities while prohibiting fee denials of communicable disease services.

headings.title: Publication and distribution of county orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires county health orders to be filed with the county clerk, made publicly available, and published in local newspapers for three consecutive weeks.

headings.title: Criminal misdemeanor penalties for order violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violations of published county health orders as misdemeanors and authorizes county commissions and health boards to initiate prosecutions.

headings.title: Compliance with emergency health order limitations
headings.reviewNote: Requires all county public health orders and regulations promulgated under this section to comply with political subdivision emergency laws.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes county commissions and health boards to promulgate public health orders, establish fees, publish orders, and enforce misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Establishment of Document Services Fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Department of Health and Senior Services Document Services Fund funded by publication, document, and data reproduction fees.

headings.title: Exemption from general revenue lapse up to fifty thousand
headings.reviewNote: Exempts an unexpended balance in the fund at fiscal year end not exceeding fifty thousand dollars from section 33.080 transfer to the general revenue fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates the Department of Health and Senior Services Document Services Fund funded by document fees and exempts up to fifty thousand dollars of unexpended year-end balance from general revenue lapse.

headings.title: Active duty military professional license good standing
headings.reviewNote: Requires health-related professional licensing boards to keep active duty military members in good professional standing during activation.

headings.title: Waiver of renewal fees and continuing education
headings.reviewNote: Requires military professional licenses to be renewed without fees, dues, or continuing education where military duties or deployment prevent compliance.

headings.title: Duration of military license continuation protections
headings.reviewNote: Continues professional licenses throughout active military duty and for at least six months following release from active service.

entries.reviewSummary: Protects professional licensure good standing, waives renewal fees, and suspends continuing education for military personnel on active duty.

headings.title: Definitions for maternal and neonatal designations
headings.reviewNote: Defines birthing facility and department for maternal and neonatal care designation provisions.

headings.title: Criteria for maternal and neonatal care designations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to establish maternal and neonatal care level criteria based on AAP and ACOG standards following public hearings.

headings.title: Construction regarding professional health care licensure
headings.reviewNote: Provides that maternal and neonatal designation standards shall not modify or expand existing healthcare professional licensure.

headings.title: Construction regarding patient transfer requirements
headings.reviewNote: Provides that designation standards shall not be construed to require that a patient be transferred to a different facility.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Directs promulgation of maternal and neonatal designation rules subject to statutory nonseverability requirements under chapter 536.

headings.title: Reporting requirements for hospital birthing facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires any hospital with a birthing facility, beginning January 1, 2019, to report its appropriate maternal and neonatal care designation levels to the department.

headings.title: Reporting by state university birthing facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires any state university hospital with a birthing facility, beginning January 1, 2019, to report its appropriate maternal and neonatal care designation levels to the department.

headings.title: Partnerships with national professional standards bodies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to partner with recognized national professional healthcare organizations with expertise in maternal and neonatal standards.

headings.title: Exclusion of pregnancy termination from criteria
headings.reviewNote: Excludes pregnancy termination and counseling or referral for pregnancy termination from the maternal and neonatal care level criteria.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes criteria for levels of maternal and neonatal care designations, hospital reporting, national partnerships, and exclusion of pregnancy termination.

headings.title: Creation of Senior Services Growth and Development Program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Senior Services Growth and Development Program to provide dedicated state funding for senior services through area agencies on aging.

headings.title: Premium tax allocation for senior services
headings.reviewNote: Allocates a percentage of insurance premium taxes to the senior services fund, rising to five percent annually beginning January 2021.

headings.title: Establishment of dedicated senior services fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Senior Services Growth and Development Program Fund as a dedicated nonreverting treasury fund solely for area agency services.

headings.title: Disbursement formula for area agencies on aging
headings.reviewNote: Directs disbursement of senior program fund moneys to area agencies on aging under the department's established federal and state funding formula.

headings.title: Allocation requirement for senior center programs
