headings.reviewNote: Mandates that at least fifty percent of distributed moneys be applied by area agencies to develop and expand senior center programs and facilities.

headings.title: Annual reporting on program fund distribution
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual reports on fund distribution and usage by area agencies to the department, insurance department, and general assembly.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department rulemaking to implement senior growth program provisions subject to chapter 536 nonseverability requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Senior Services Growth and Development Program, allocates premium taxes, funds senior center services, and requires annual reports.

headings.title: State coverage for amino acid elemental formulas
headings.reviewNote: Requires coverage for the full cost of amino acid-based elemental formulas for children under nineteen with severe diagnosed digestive disorders.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants the department rulemaking authority to implement formula coverage provisions subject to chapter 536 nonseverability requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates state coverage for amino acid-based elemental formulas for diagnosed pediatric gastrointestinal disorders, subject to appropriations.

headings.title: Registration requirement for radiation sources and machines
headings.reviewNote: Makes it unlawful to produce radiation, use radioactive materials, or operate radiation machines without registering with the department.

headings.title: Compliance requirement with radiation control standards
headings.reviewNote: Makes it unlawful to produce radiation or store radioactive materials except in compliance with statutory radiation control standards and regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits unregistered radiation production or radioactive material usage and mandates compliance with radiation safety laws.

headings.title: Notice and order to abate radiation violations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to issue written notice and order abatement within thirty days upon finding radiation safety violations.

headings.title: Department right of entry for radiation inspections
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department enforcement agents free access and entry at reasonable times to buildings for radiation inspection and examination.

headings.title: Confidentiality of radiation data and investigations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to keep confidential all data obtained from radiation source registrations, inspections, and investigations.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes radiation violation abatement orders, inspector right of entry, and establishes confidentiality of radiation data.

headings.title: Criminal misdemeanor penalties and civil injunctions
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violations of radiation control laws or rules as misdemeanors and authorizes civil injunctions to restrain violations.

headings.title: Daily offenses for ongoing radiation violations
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that each day a radiation violation continues shall constitute a separate statutory offense.

headings.title: Injunctive relief actions by attorney general
headings.reviewNote: Directs the attorney general upon department request to commence civil actions for injunctive relief to prevent radiation violations.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes criminal penalties for radiation violations, defines separate daily offenses, and authorizes injunctive relief by the attorney general.

headings.title: Definitions for dental radiation imaging systems
headings.reviewNote: Defines cone beam computed tomography system and panoramic x-ray system for radiation inspection provisions.

headings.title: Triennial inspection interval for low-intensity systems
headings.reviewNote: Exempts dental cone beam and panoramic systems producing thirty milligrays or less from inspections more frequent than triennial.

headings.title: Annual inspection requirement for high-intensity systems
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual inspections for cone beam computed tomography systems producing radiation intensity exceeding thirty milligrays.

headings.title: Inspections upon installation or relocation in office
headings.reviewNote: Requires all cone beam computed tomography systems and panoramic x-ray systems to be inspected within thirty days of installation and whenever moved within an office.

headings.title: Quadrennial inspection limit for veterinary x-ray equipment
headings.reviewNote: Exempts conventional x-ray equipment used exclusively on animals by a licensed veterinarian or veterinary facility under chapter 340 from inspections more frequent than every four years.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates inspection intervals for cone beam computed tomography systems, panoramic x-ray systems, and conventional veterinary x-ray equipment.

headings.title: Establishment and composition of advisory committee
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Advisory Committee on Childhood Immunization within the department and specifies professional and geographic regional membership.

headings.title: Mandatory regional public meetings on immunization
headings.reviewNote: Requires regional committee members to organize and participate in public meetings within their regions to gather childhood immunization information.

headings.title: Member terms and duties of advisory committee
headings.reviewNote: Establishes three-year terms and expense reimbursement without compensation, and tasks the committee with evaluating record systems, under-five data entry, confidential analysis, and immunization plans (source footnote notes 'a' in original rolls).

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Advisory Committee on Childhood Immunization, defining membership, regional meetings, and advisory duties.

headings.title: Establishment of cancer information reporting system
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to establish and maintain a cancer information reporting system to collect data for federal grant compliance.

headings.title: Neoplasm reporting rules for inpatient and outpatient care
headings.reviewNote: Directs rulemaking prescribing reportable malignant neoplasms, data items, and six-month reporting deadlines for inpatient and outpatient facilities.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs establishment and maintenance of a cancer information reporting system and specifies reporting rules for neoplasms.

headings.title: Mandatory facility reporting of malignant neoplasms
headings.reviewNote: Requires administrators of hospitals, clinics, laboratories, and long-term care facilities to report diagnosed malignant neoplasms to the department.

headings.title: Physician duty to provide diagnostic information
headings.reviewNote: Requires attending physicians and diagnosing providers to provide necessary neoplasm case information to the facility administrator.

headings.title: Submission of cancer data through designated systems
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes submitting cancer reporting data through data systems designated by the reporting entity or individual.

headings.title: Exemption from duplicate centralized reporting
headings.reviewNote: Provides that facilities submitting cancer cases through centralized department reporting systems are exempt from duplicate reporting.

entries.reviewSummary: Mandates cancer case reporting by healthcare facilities, physician data disclosures, and submission through centralized systems.

headings.title: Confidentiality and protected identities in cancer reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to protect identities of patients, physicians, and reporting facilities, prohibiting release without written consent.

headings.title: Research criteria for requesting identity release
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department consent requests for identity disclosure only upon showing that patient and facility identities are necessary for research.

headings.title: Educational reports and researcher data access
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to use or publish cancer reports to advance research, education, and treatment, and to provide data to qualified researchers complying with rule conditions and paying processing fees.

headings.title: Data exchange agreements with other cancer registries
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes data exchange agreements with governmental cancer registries provided recipient registries maintain identical identity protections.

entries.reviewSummary: Protects confidentiality of cancer registry data, regulates patient and facility consent for disclosures, and authorizes data exchanges.

headings.title: Immunity from liability for reporting cancer data
headings.reviewNote: Protects individuals and organizations from civil and criminal liability for providing cancer data absent bad faith or malicious purpose.

headings.title: Protection against compelled medical examination or treatment
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that cancer reporting provisions shall not be construed to compel any individual to submit to medical examination or treatment.

headings.title: Infraction penalty for cancer reporting violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies any violation of statutory cancer reporting and confidentiality provisions as an infraction.

entries.reviewSummary: Provides civil and criminal immunity for cancer reporting, protects individual rights against compelled examination, and sets infraction penalties.

headings.title: Annual hospital charge and patient abstract reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires healthcare providers and hospitals to provide annual charge, patient abstract, and financial data to the department.

headings.title: Collection of healthcare-associated infection data
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to collect infection incidence data from hospitals, ambulatory surgical centers, and abortion facilities.

headings.title: Rulemaking for infection data collection and analysis
headings.reviewNote: Directs promulgation of rules establishing standards for infection data collection, analysis, risk adjustment, and public reporting.

headings.title: Evaluation of federal infection reporting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to evaluate CMS infection data collection requirements to avoid duplicate reporting burdens on hospitals.

headings.title: National Healthcare Safety Network guideline implementation
headings.reviewNote: Directs implementation of CDC National Healthcare Safety Network guidelines as a mandatory condition of facility licensure.

headings.title: Exemption from duplicative data resubmission
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits requiring facilities to resubmit data already provided to health or social services under other statutory provisions.

headings.title: Confidentiality of infection data and report disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Classifies raw infection data as nonpublic information while permitting published reports that identify individual healthcare facilities.

headings.title: Publication of consumer guides and comparative studies
headings.reviewNote: Directs publication of comparative healthcare studies and an annual consumer guide developed in collaboration with stakeholders.

headings.title: Sanctions and program exclusion for noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits providers that continually and substantially fail to comply with reporting rules from participating in state-funded programs.

headings.title: Administrative appeal of state money ineligibility
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes hospitals under section 197.071 and ambulatory surgical centers or abortion facilities under section 197.221 to appeal department determinations of ineligibility for state moneys.

headings.title: Rulemaking for infection reporting by other facilities
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes rules establishing infection reporting and publication standards for other health facility types based on public health need.

headings.title: Specific healthcare-associated infection reporting categories
headings.reviewNote: Directs regulatory adoption of reporting standards for specified surgical site, bloodstream, and central line-associated infections.

headings.title: Annual facility-specific infection rate reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual public reports based on twelve-month compiled data showing facility-specific infection rates and comparisons.

headings.title: Alignment with national infection tracking standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires reported infection types to remain consistent with infections tracked by the National Healthcare Safety Network.

headings.title: Website publication and distribution of infection reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires infection reports to be published on the department website and distributed annually to the governor and general assembly.

headings.title: Standardized quality measure compliance reporting
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Hospital Industry Data Institute to publish annual compliance reports on standardized quality measures for facilities.

headings.title: Use of infection data for facility licensing
headings.reviewNote: Makes collected infection data available to the department for licensing hospitals, surgical centers, and abortion facilities.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and statutory nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Grants rulemaking authority to implement infection reporting provisions subject to chapter 536 nonseverability requirements.

headings.title: Mandatory hospital antimicrobial stewardship programs
headings.reviewNote: Requires hospitals (excluding chapter 632 mental health facilities), ambulatory surgical centers, and abortion facilities to establish antimicrobial stewardship programs monitored by quality improvement departments.

headings.title: Electronic reporting of antimicrobial usage and resistance
headings.reviewNote: Requires electronic reporting of antimicrobial usage and resistance data through the CDC module once federal standards take effect.

headings.title: Annual legislative report on antimicrobial resistance
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to report annually to the general assembly regarding antimicrobial-resistant infection incidence across regions.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates healthcare-associated infection reporting, public report publishing, sanction standards, and mandatory antimicrobial stewardship programs.

headings.title: Establishment of regional arthritis programs
headings.reviewNote: Establishes regional arthritis programs within the department, subject to appropriations, to improve arthritis management and care access.

headings.title: Patient, family, and public arthritis education
headings.reviewNote: Requires established regional arthritis programs to operate education programs for patients, families, and the general public.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes regional arthritis programs within the department and mandates public and patient education activities.

headings.title: Authorization to manufacture and use DMSO
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the manufacture, distribution, sale, possession, and medical use of DMSO in Missouri for arthritis treatment.

headings.title: Definition of DMSO substance
headings.reviewNote: Defines DMSO as a product containing dimethyl sulfoxide or its derivatives as its primary chemical component.

headings.title: Physician disciplinary protection for prescribing DMSO
headings.reviewNote: Protects licensed physicians from disciplinary action by the healing arts board for prescribing DMSO according to medical standards.

headings.title: Nurse disciplinary protection for administering DMSO
headings.reviewNote: Protects licensed nurses from disciplinary action by the nursing board for administering DMSO under physician direction and medical standards.

headings.title: Pharmacist disciplinary protection for dispensing DMSO
headings.reviewNote: Protects licensed pharmacists from pharmacy board discipline for dispensing DMSO pursuant to a valid prescription under professional standards.

headings.title: Prohibition against facility restriction of DMSO
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits hospitals and healthcare facilities from interfering with physician-patient decisions by restricting or forbidding prescribed DMSO use.

headings.title: Professional standard of care and malpractice
headings.reviewNote: Provides that prescribing or dispensing DMSO according to acceptable professional standards does not in itself constitute malpractice.

headings.title: Mandatory product warning label on DMSO
headings.reviewNote: Requires all DMSO manufactured or distributed in Missouri to bear a prominent state disclaimer and arthritis use warning label.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes DMSO use for arthritis, shields medical professionals from discipline, bans facility interference, and mandates product warning labels.

headings.title: Confidentiality of head injury reports and records
headings.reviewNote: Classifies all head and spinal cord injury registry reports as confidential records restricted to department staff and approved researchers.

headings.title: Protection of patient and facility identities
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits disclosing patient, physician, or hospital identities without written consent from the individual or reporting facility.

headings.title: Research justification required for identity release
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants seeking identifiable registry data to establish that identity disclosure is necessary for worthwhile research.

headings.title: Annual statistical report on traumatic injuries
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to compile and submit an annual statistical report on head and spinal cord injury registry data.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes confidentiality protections for head and spinal cord injury reports, regulates research access, and requires annual statistical reports.

headings.title: Protection against compelled medical examination or treatment
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that head injury registry provisions shall not be construed to compel any individual to submit to examination or treatment.

headings.title: Infraction penalty for injury registry violations
headings.reviewNote: Classifies any violation of statutory head and spinal cord injury registry provisions as an infraction.

entries.reviewSummary: Prohibits compelled medical examination under injury registry provisions and classifies registry violations as infractions.

headings.title: Establishment of Missouri Brain Injury Advisory Council
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri Brain Injury Advisory Council within the department, providing for three-year staggered member terms.

headings.title: Department administrative support and appropriations
headings.reviewNote: Assigns the council to the department and directs submission of budget estimates for necessary administrative appropriations.

headings.title: Council meetings and chairperson election
headings.reviewNote: Requires council meetings at least four times annually and provides for council election of a chairperson.

headings.title: Member expense reimbursement without compensation
headings.reviewNote: Provides that council members serve without compensation but shall, subject to appropriations, be reimbursed for actual and necessary expenses.

headings.title: Adoption of written governance procedures
headings.reviewNote: Requires the council to adopt written governance procedures to regulate its advisory activities and meetings.

headings.title: Recommendations for statewide brain injury service plan
headings.reviewNote: Directs the council to formulate recommendations to the department director for developing a statewide brain injury service plan.

headings.title: Conflict of interest restrictions for council members
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits council members from voting on or seeking to influence decisions in which they hold direct professional or financial interests.

headings.title: Advisory duties and educational program promotion
headings.reviewNote: Delineates council advisory duties to promote educational programs, disseminate information, and encourage prevention of traumatic brain injuries.

headings.title: Acceptance of grants and gift contributions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to accept federal funds, foundation grants, private gifts, and donations on behalf of the council.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Missouri Brain Injury Advisory Council, defining membership, meetings, advisory duties, conflict rules, and funding.

headings.title: Rulemaking for radiation machine licensing and registration
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate rules providing for licensing, registration, and regulatory exemptions for radiation machines.

headings.title: Intentional medical exposure exemption for research
headings.reviewNote: Provides that radiation rules shall not limit intentional patient radiation exposure for lawful medical therapy or research.

headings.title: Operator training and performance standards for mammography
headings.reviewNote: Requires department rules establishing minimum training, education, and performance standards for individuals operating mammography machines.

headings.title: Avoidance of dual licensing and interstate recognition
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to avoid dual licensing burdens and authorizes acceptance of comparable federal or state credentials.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs rulemaking for radiation machine licensing, training standards for mammography operators, and avoidance of dual licensing.

headings.title: Fee schedules for radiation source licensing
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to establish administrative fee schedules for specific radiation source licensing by rule.

headings.title: Assessment of nonrefundable mammography inspection fees
headings.reviewNote: Establishes statutory inspection, reinspection, and authorization fee amounts for radiation machines used to perform mammography.

headings.title: Evaluation fee waiver for ACR accreditation
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to waive the subsection 2 compliance evaluation fee when a mammography authorization applicant submits an American College of Radiology accreditation certificate evidencing compliance.

headings.title: Creation of Mammography Fund and nonreversion
headings.reviewNote: Requires depositing all section fees with the state treasurer in the dedicated Mammography Fund, exempt from biennial transfer to general revenue under section 33.080.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes radiation licensing fee schedules, nonrefundable mammography inspection fees, ACR accreditation evaluation fee waivers, and the nonreverting Mammography Fund.

headings.title: Mammography machine registration and authorization requirement
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using radiation machines for mammography without registration and authorization from the department of health.

headings.title: Technical standards for mammography authorization
headings.reviewNote: Specifies seven authorization standards including ACR accreditation criteria, DHSS machine and facility rules, mammography-specific design and exclusive use, annual physicist consultation with sixty-month records, dose rules, and trained operators (source footnotes note clerical section-number errors in original rolls).

headings.title: Issuance of temporary mammography authorization permits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes issuance of nonrenewable temporary permits allowing machine operation while evidence of compliance is submitted.

headings.title: Application procedures for mammography machine authorization
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes application procedures, machine identifying data, and documentation required to obtain mammography authorization.

headings.title: Annual inspection requirement for mammography equipment
headings.reviewNote: Directs annual (and permits more frequent) department inspections of mammography machines and requires reasonable efforts to coordinate with the department's other facility inspections.

headings.title: Issuance and posting of inspection certificates
headings.reviewNote: Requires issuance of inspection certificates upon satisfactory review and mandates prominent posting near the mammography machine.

headings.title: Grounds for withdrawal of mammography authorization
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes withdrawal of mammography authorization if equipment fails to meet technical standards or safety rules.

headings.title: Notice and hearing rights upon authorization denial
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees applicants and machine owners an administrative hearing before authorization denial or withdrawal becomes final.

headings.title: Emergency order removing machine from service
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes immediate emergency orders removing mammography machines from service when critical safety defects pose public health risks.

headings.title: Prohibition on machine use following withdrawal
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits using radiation machines for mammography following authorization withdrawal until full compliance is demonstrated.

headings.title: Sanctions and reinspection fees for unauthorized operations
headings.reviewNote: Assesses additional reinspection fees and administrative sanctions against persons operating mammography machines without authorization.

headings.title: Injunctive actions by attorney general to restrain violations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the attorney general to institute civil actions for injunctive relief to stop unlawful mammography machine use.

headings.title: Alignment with federal Medicare mammography rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires state mammography rules to be fairly consistent with Health Care Financing Administration rules for Medicare coverage of screening mammography under the Omnibus Reconciliation Act of 1990.

entries.reviewSummary: Regulates mammography machine registration, authorization standards, annual inspections, emergency shut-down orders, and enforcement.

headings.title: State coverage of COVID-19 testing out-of-pocket costs
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department payment of uncovered patient copayments and deductibles for COVID-19 testing up to one hundred fifty dollars per test.

headings.title: Prohibition against insurer reduction of COVID-19 testing coverage
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits health insurers from reducing insurance coverage for COVID-19 testing during declared gubernatorial states of emergency.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes state coverage for resident COVID-19 testing copayments and deductibles and prohibits insurer reduction of testing coverage.

headings.title: Adolescent weight loss pill education program
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to implement an education program highlighting the risks of over-the-counter weight loss pills for minors.

headings.title: Public awareness strategies and media outreach campaigns
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes public service announcements, advertisements, community forums, and health fairs to increase awareness of weight loss pill risks.

headings.title: Interagency collaboration for educational distribution
headings.reviewNote: Directs elementary and secondary education to collaborate with the department in distributing weight loss pill educational materials.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority under administrative procedures act
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to promulgate rules under chapter 536 to carry out the weight loss pill awareness program.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs implementation of an adolescent weight loss pill education program, outreach campaigns, interagency collaboration, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Elder abuse and financial exploitation awareness program
headings.reviewNote: Requires an education program to reduce elder abuse and financial exploitation through mandatory reporter training and hotline publicity.

headings.title: Interagency cooperation and distribution by licensed facilities
headings.reviewNote: Requires social services and licensed healthcare and long-term care facilities to cooperate in distributing elder abuse materials.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs implementation of an elder abuse, neglect, and financial exploitation awareness program and interagency information distribution.

headings.title: Establishment of Money Follows the Person committee
headings.reviewNote: Directs establishment of an interagency committee to assess continuation of the Money Follows the Person demonstration program.

headings.title: Program evaluation duties of demonstration committee
headings.reviewNote: Directs the committee to review program achievements, evaluate improvements, investigate sustainability costs, and explore waiver options.

headings.title: Composition and agency membership of committee
headings.reviewNote: Specifies committee membership including fiscal staff from social services, health, mental health, budget, legislative members, and councils.

headings.title: Inclusion of additional stakeholders and work groups
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the committee to include additional members and work groups representing state agencies, community groups, and legislators.

headings.title: Recommendations and final report to general assembly
headings.reviewNote: Requires social services in cooperation with health and mental health to submit recommendations and findings to the legislature by July 2016.

headings.title: Statutory expiration date of demonstration committee
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the statutory provisions governing the Money Follows the Person study committee shall expire on January 1, 2017.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes a temporary interagency committee to evaluate the Money Follows the Person demonstration program, report findings, and sunset in 2017.

headings.title: Establishment of Pregnancy-Associated Mortality Review Board
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Pregnancy-Associated Mortality Review Board within the department to improve data collection and reporting on maternal deaths.

headings.title: Definitions for pregnancy mortality review provisions
headings.reviewNote: Defines department, maternal death, and maternity care deserts for pregnancy-associated mortality review provisions.

headings.title: Board membership size, meetings, and staggered terms
headings.reviewNote: Specifies a board of up to twenty-two members meeting at least semiannually and serving four-year staggered terms appointed by the director.

headings.title: Multidisciplinary membership and geographic diversity standards
headings.reviewNote: Requires diverse multidisciplinary board representation across medical specialties, public health, congressional districts, and rural and urban areas.

headings.title: Powers and duties of mortality review board
headings.reviewNote: Directs comprehensive reviews of maternal deaths, identification of maternity care deserts, analysis of disparities, and prevention recommendations.

headings.title: Board contracting authority for review operations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the board to enter into contracts with external entities consistent with statutory review responsibilities.

headings.title: Annual maternal mortality report and website publication
headings.reviewNote: Requires an annual report on maternal mortality disaggregated by demographic factors submitted to the CDC, governor, legislature, and public website.

headings.title: Department provision of vital records to board
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department director to provide the board with death certificates and linked birth or fetal death records for maternal deaths.

headings.title: Mandatory data submissions by healthcare providers
headings.reviewNote: Requires providers, facilities, and law enforcement to provide records relating to maternal deaths occurring within twenty-four months.

headings.title: Confidentiality and legal discovery protections for records
headings.reviewNote: Protects all board proceedings, interviews, and mortality data as strictly confidential and inadmissible in civil or criminal proceedings.

headings.title: Grant funding and gift acceptance authorization
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to use grant funds and accept private, foundation, local, or federal moneys to support board operations.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Pregnancy-Associated Mortality Review Board, defining duties, membership, reporting, vital record access, and confidentiality protections.
